national_raw_news.title: HM Amit Shah inaugurates 12th NDRF Battalion campus in Arunachal Pradesh
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the campus of the 12th Battalion of the National Disaster Response Force in Hollongi, near Itanagar in Arunachal Pradesh today. The new campus is aimed at strengthening disaster management infrastructure and improving the NDRF’s preparedness and response capabilities in Arunachal Pradesh and other parts of the Northeast. Describing the Northeast as highly vulnerable to natural disasters, Mr Shah said the battalion would serve not only Arunachal Pradesh but also the entire Northeast and neighbouring regions. He said strengthening disaster preparedness, promoting economic self-reliance and ensuring better livelihood opportunities would remain important priorities in the development of Arunachal Pradesh and the Northeast. Mr Shah appreciated the decision of the NDRF Director General to open the Olympic-size swimming pool to swimming enthusiasts and athletes of Itanagar and Arunachal Pradesh free of cost. Earlier in the day, Mr. Shah launched the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision Document 2027 and inaugurated the Saras Mela at the Dorjee Khandu State Convention Centre in Itanagar. He also flagged off a Mobile Medical Van and interacted with members of women Self-Help Groups and cooperative societies. The event also saw the launch of several development initiatives worth over 5,600 crore rupees, covering education, power, rural roads and border-area development. Addressing the Conference, the Cooperation Minister said, the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) have been advised to procure agricultural produce directly from farmers in Arunachal Pradesh. He said the initiative would provide better market opportunities and financial benefits to local farmers while ensuring the availability of quality products for security forces. He said, such initiatives would also strengthen the bond of trust and cooperation between security forces and the local population. Emphasising the need to strengthen self-reliance, the Minister said the State and the country must move forward by strengthening initiatives such as the Swavalamban Yojana. He urged the State Government to ensure that employment opportunities and the benefits of development reach every citizen.

national_raw_news.title: IFFI screens ‘Naqsh-e-Daur’, exploring Kashmir’s woodcarving heritage 3 hours ago 61
national_raw_news.content: Day 3 at the 57th edition of IFFI also saw the screening of the film Naqsh-e-Daur, directed by Baba Tasadduq Hussain and produced by Bharat Bala which explores the rich artistic heritage of Kashmir through the life and work of renowned woodcarver and Padma Shri awardee Ghulam Nabi Dar. Naqsh-e-Daur tells the story of Padma Shri Ghulam Nabi Dar, who has been carving stories on wood. For him, woodcarving is not just a craft but “ibaadat” or worship. In an exclusive interview to Akashvani, the two share their vision behind telling the story of a woodcarver. Director Baba Tasadduq Hussain said that making a film about an art form rooted in his own homeland was both challenging and deeply personal. He credited producer Bharat Bala for guiding him in discovering the cinematic potential of the story and shaping its visual language. Bharatbala, is one of India’s most distinctive filmmakers. He is particularly celebrated for creating cinematic works that capture India’s cultural identity, patriotism, history and diversity through powerful visuals and music. The soul-stirring visuals he created in Maa Tujhe Salam, coupled with A. R. Rahman’s music still make one’s heart swell with pride. He founded Virtual Bharat, in which he produces films telling stories of ordinary men in an extraordinary way. Veteran actor and Jury Member of Prasar Bharati’s Page Se Pitch Tak initiative, Manoj Joshi has emphasised the importance of promoting original stories rooted in India’s culture, traditions and local experiences. Talking to Akashvani News, he said that the initiative would encourage young writers to bring stories from their own regions to the screen. He noted that with audiences increasingly exposed to films from across the world, there is a need to showcase authentic Indian stories rather than rely on copied narratives.

national_raw_news.title: India shifts healthcare research focus towards prevention, precision medicine: Dr Jitendra Singh
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) Science and Technology Dr Jitendra Singh on Sunday said India’s healthcare research approach is increasingly shifting towards prevention, early detection and advanced research at molecular and genetic levels, as lifestyle-related and metabolic disorders continue to affect younger populations. Addressing THE WEEK Health Summit 2026 in New Delhi, the Minister said healthcare was moving beyond conventional treatment methods towards scientific interventions and more precise disease management, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. He highlighted the growing prevalence of diabetes, obesity, hypertension and cardiovascular diseases among young people, attributing the trend to changing dietary habits, declining physical activity and lifestyle-related risks. Emphasising the importance of preventive healthcare, Singh said addressing these challenges requires greater public awareness and collective participation, rather than relying solely on medical professionals. The Minister said advances in biotechnology, molecular science and genetic research were opening new possibilities for understanding diseases and developing targeted treatment strategies. Highlighting India’s progress in genomics, he said genome sequencing of 10,000 individuals belonging to 84 different populations had been undertaken to better understand the country’s genetic diversity, disease susceptibility and healthcare risks. The study has identified more than 400 genetic traits across different populations, he added. Singh also highlighted the government’s HPV vaccination initiative, under which more than 50 lakh adolescent girls have been vaccinated as part of efforts to prevent cervical cancer. He recalled India’s development of an indigenous DNA vaccine during the COVID-19 pandemic as an important milestone in the country’s vaccine research capabilities. Referring to precision medicine, the Minister said treatment approaches were increasingly being tailored to an individual’s genetic profile, lifestyle and environment, recognising that the same disease may require different treatment strategies for different people. He also highlighted research into biomarkers among women with gestational diabetes to identify those at higher risk of developing Type 2 diabetes later in life. On rare genetic diseases, Singh said the government and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) were working to expand access to diagnosis and treatment and make therapies more affordable. He further referred to indigenous medical research, including the development of new antibiotics and advances in genetic therapies. Citing gene therapy research for haemophilia conducted by Christian Medical College, Vellore, and published in the New England Journal of Medicine, he said Indian researchers were developing advanced medical solutions with potential applications beyond the country. The Minister also highlighted the expansion of dialysis facilities in district hospitals and ongoing research into the early detection of kidney diseases, even before symptoms emerge. Calling for stronger collaboration among government institutions, research organisations, healthcare professionals and private-sector partners, Singh said such partnerships were essential to translate scientific discoveries into accessible healthcare solutions. He also cautioned young people against health-related misinformation, unverified nutrition advice and the unsupervised use of medicines for cosmetic purposes, urging them to rely on qualified medical professionals and credible scientific information. -Pib

national_raw_news.title: HM Amit Shah stresses stronger security coordination in Arunachal Pradesh
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has stressed the need for better coordination between Central and State security agencies to maintain peace and security in Arunachal Pradesh. He called for strengthening the local intelligence network and ensuring continuous monitoring of sensitive areas. Considering the strategic importance of Arunachal Pradesh’s nearly 1,126-kilometre-long international border with China, Mr. Shah also reviewed border security arrangements and the development of strategic infrastructure along the frontier. Mr. Shah chaired a high-level review meeting at Lok Bhavan in Itanagar yesterday to discuss key issues relating to law and order, internal security, border management and development in the Northeastern state. The Home Minister also emphasised expanding road connectivity, border outposts, helipads and telecommunication facilities in border areas. He stressed the effective implementation of the Vibrant Villages Programme to enhance livelihood opportunities for local residents. Mr. Shah said that under Mission Krishi Veer and Mission Arun Himveer, a distinct approach should be adopted, under which the requirements of security forces are assessed first and local villages are subsequently equipped to fulfil those needs. Chief Minister Pema Khandu thanked the Union Home Minister for his guidance and assured him that the state government would make every effort to implement the directives and accelerate the state’s development.

national_raw_news.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to arrive in New Delhi today on a two-day visit to India
national_raw_news.content: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will be on a two-day visit to India from today. This will be his first visit to India after assuming office in March this year. On his arrival in New Delhi today, he will hold meeting with External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar. Tomorrow, the Nepal Prime Minister will call on President Droupadi Murmu and also meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi. During the bilateral talks, both Prime Ministers will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) in various areas will also be exchanged between the two countries. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the Ministry of External Affairs has said that the visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal under its ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. It added that the visit will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the bilateral partnership and advance mutually beneficial cooperation. The Ministry further said that India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors including trade and commerce, energy and water resources, and digital connectivity. The two countries also witnessed growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi calls for greater respect for skills, says India moving towards becoming global skill capital
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday participated in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, and called for greater recognition of skilled workers, saying India’s progress in the 21st century depends on respecting skills and craftsmanship. Addressing the gathering, PM Modi said the government had undertaken several initiatives guided by the principle of ‘Shrameva Jayate’ to strengthen skill development and create employment opportunities for young people. He said ITI graduates were now ready to contribute directly to nation-building, adding that skilled workers play a crucial role in strengthening India’s manufacturing capacity and making people’s lives easier. Highlighting India’s traditional craftsmanship, the Prime Minister cited Chikankari, Banarasi silk, Kashmir Pashmina, Kalamkari and other indigenous crafts, saying skills had long been central to the country’s identity and economy. He attributed the decline in the recognition of skilled professions to the colonial education system, which, he said, promoted clerical jobs at the expense of traditional crafts. PM Modi said nearly 5,000 new Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) had been established over the past decade, while enrolment had increased by more than five lakh. The number of girls pursuing ITI education has also risen more than two-and-a-half times, he added. Emphasising the need to align vocational training with emerging technologies, he said more than 30 new-age trades, including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, drone technology, electric vehicles, industrial robotics, green hydrogen and semiconductor technology, had been introduced in ITIs. The Prime Minister also highlighted an investment of Rs 60,000 crore under the PM-SETU scheme to modernise ITI infrastructure, upgrade machinery, train instructors and strengthen industry linkages. Addressing concerns over artificial intelligence replacing jobs, PM Modi said skilled workers would continue to have employment opportunities, citing their contribution during the COVID-19 pandemic. He said emerging sectors such as renewable energy, sports manufacturing and infrastructure were generating growing demand for skilled manpower. Announcing a major opportunity for Indian youth, the Prime Minister said India would host the WorldSkills Asia competition in Greater Noida in 2027, bringing together participants from several countries. He also highlighted Uttar Pradesh’s development under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, citing expressways, international airports, educational institutions, mobile manufacturing facilities and the upcoming semiconductor factory as drivers of employment and investment. Urging young people to pursue skill development and aim high, PM Modi said India was moving towards becoming the skill capital of the world. He encouraged ITI graduates to make full use of emerging opportunities and contribute to the vision of a developed India. PIB

The tool lets doctors dictate prescriptions directly into the hospital’s electronic system during outpatient consultations. Government-backed language AI platform BHASHINI’s voice prescription tool is moving from a two-department pilot to an institute-wide rollout at AIIMS New Delhi, a Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology release said on Saturday. AIIMS has integrated BHASHINI’s speech-to-text technology into the National Informatics Centre’s eHospital prescription module. The tool lets doctors dictate prescriptions directly into the hospital’s electronic system during outpatient consultations. “The platform has proved useful in supporting clinical workflows, with positive feedback from doctors during the pilot in Neurology and Neurosurgery. Building on this experience, the application is now being rolled out across the institute,” said Prof Vivek Tandon, professor in charge of the computer facility at AIIMS New Delhi. The rollout was highlighted at the Global Digital Health Summit in New Delhi, where BHASHINI also showcased how JIPMER and the Indian Army are using voice AI in their existing hospital systems. The Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER) has integrated BHASHINI into its e-Sushrut hospital management system. Doctors can dictate case histories, inpatient notes and discharge instructions in English or supported Indian languages. Dr Anand A of JIPMER said the institute aims to “make clinical workflows more efficient and reduce documentation burdens on healthcare professionals.” The Army’s Directorate General of Medical Services demonstrated how its Dhanwantri system converts doctors’ spoken clinical notes into typed text. Maj Gen Sandeep Bhalla said the Army sought multilingual support because its patients, including serving personnel, veterans and their families, speak different languages. Private hospitals have also been exploring voice-based prescribing. Global Health Ltd, which operates Medanta hospitals, said in its FY2024–25 annual report that it was implementing an AI-based electronic medical records platform with a feature that transcribes and categorises spoken prescriptions. The Union Health Ministry also showcased a voice-to-text prescription tool integrated into a hospital management system at the India AI Impact Expo in February 2026. national_raw_news.title: President Murmu condoles loss of lives in car-truck collision in Gujarat's Kutch - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: President Murmu condoles loss of lives in car-truck collision in Gujarat's Kutch Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर President Murmu condoles loss of lives in car-truck collision in Gujarat's Kutch ANI | Updated: Nov 22, 2026 16:18 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 22 (ANI): President Droupadi Murmu expressed deep sorrow over the tragic road accident in Gujarat’s Kutch district, which claimed the lives of seven people. Taking to the social media platform X, President Murmu extended her condolences to the families of the victims. "The news of the deaths in a road accident in Kutch , Gujarat, is deeply saddening. I express my heartfelt condolences to all the bereaved family members of the deceased," the President said in her post. According to police officials, at least seven people, including three children and two women, were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a truck on the Bhuj-Khavda highway near Vekariya Rann in Kutch district. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) for the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives, while those injured in the accident will receive Rs 50,000 each. “Saddened by the loss of lives due to a mishap in Kutch , Gujarat. My condolences to those who have lost their loved ones. Praying for the speedy recovery of the injured,” PM said. Announcing financial assistance for the affected families, the PMO said, “An ex-gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs. 50,000.” According to Kutch Superintendent of Police Vikas Sunda, the accident occurred between 9.30 pm and 10 pm on November 21 when a car travelling from Khavda towards Bhuj collided with a truck coming from the opposite direction. "On the night of November 21, 2026, between 9:30 PM and 10:00 PM, a tragic incident occurred on the Bhuj-Khavda highway. A car travelling from Khavda toward Bhuj collided with a truck moving from Bhuj toward Khavda,” he said. Preliminary observations suggest that the collision occurred while the car was attempting to overtake the truck, Sunda said. Speaking about the incident, the SP said the occupants of the car sustained injuries following the collision. A police team reached the spot and immediately initiated rescue operations, while an ambulance was also called. However, all seven occupants of the car, comprising two men, two women and three children, died in the accident. “Preliminary observations suggest that the collision occurred while the car was attempting an overtake. The occupants of the car sustained injuries. A police team arrived at the scene and immediately initiated rescue efforts. An ambulance was summoned; however, unfortunately, all seven individuals in the car—comprising two men, two women, and three children—lost their lives,” he said. national_raw_news.title: India's Barrier-Free Toll Network Expands As NHAI Activates Third MLFF Plaza In Tamil Nadu
national_raw_news.content: India's Barrier-Free Toll Network Expands As NHAI Activates Third MLFF Plaza In Tamil Nadu Infrastructure India's Barrier-Free Toll Network Expands As NHAI Activates Third MLFF Plaza In Tamil Nadu Swarajya Staff Nov 22, 2026 | Updated 12:02 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB The National Highways Authority of India has implemented its Multi-Lane Free Flow tolling system at the Chennasamudram Toll Plaza in Tamil Nadu's Ranipet district, enabling motorists to pass through without stopping at conventional toll booths. The barrier-free system, which uses FASTag and Automatic Number Plate Recognition cameras, marks Tamil Nadu's third MLFF deployment following earlier installations at Paranur and Nemili toll plazas. Located at kilometre 104.900 on National Highway 48 near Walajapet, the Chennasamudram plaza serves the busy Chennai-Bengaluru corridor. The 46.5-kilometre tollable stretch handles significant daily traffic volumes as vehicles travel between Tamil Nadu's capital and India's technology hub. The plaza features 12 toll lanes equipped with overhead cameras and RFID readers that automatically detect and deduct toll charges. The MLFF technology allows vehicles to travel at speeds up to 150 kilometres per hour while toll collection occurs seamlessly. RFID readers identify FASTag-equipped vehicles, whilst ANPR cameras capture registration plates for vehicles without valid tags. The system verifies data in real time and processes payments through linked accounts, eliminating the need for vehicles to slow down or queue at physical barriers. India's first MLFF system launched at Chorayasi Toll Plaza in Gujarat in May 2026, with the technology subsequently expanding to locations across Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi. Tamil Nadu joined the rollout when Paranur toll plaza became operational on 1 October 2026, followed by Nemili on 13 November. NHAI is deploying the system at 16 toll plazas nationwide as part of its phased implementation strategy. The barrier-free model is expected to reduce fuel consumption and vehicular emissions by eliminating idling at toll plazas. The technology also lowers operational costs associated with maintaining physical toll infrastructure whilst strengthening transparency in toll operations. Highway users must maintain valid FASTag accounts with sufficient balance to avoid electronic notices or payment-related action under the new system. national_raw_news.title: Kalai-II dam project's flawed clearances expose risks of fast-tracking SUMP
national_raw_news.content: Kalai-II dam project’s flawed clearances expose risks of fast-tracking SUMP — The Arunachal Times [email protected] Monday, 23 November 2026 [email protected] The Arunachal Times The Arunachal Times Monday, 23 November 2026, 12:17 am arunachaltimes.in State News Monday, 23 November 2026, 12:17 am • 5 min read Kalai-II dam project’s flawed clearances expose risks of fast-tracking SUMP [Badak Yomgam] On 8 April, 2026, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs cleared an investment of Rs 14,105.83 crore for the 1,200 MW Kalai-II Hydroelectric Project on the Lohit River in Arunachal Pradesh’ Anjaw district. An official Press Information Bureau (PIB) release framed the venture as a landmark step for clean power and regional connectivity. Planned as a 78-month run-of-the-river project, comprising six 190 MW units and one 60 MW unit, and executed through a joint venture between THDC India Limited (a public sector subsidiary of NTPC Limited) and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the Kalai-II dam is designed to generate 4,852.95 MU of electricity annually, strengthen state’s power supply, manage peak demand, and balance the national grid. Under the central package, Arunachal is slated to receive 12 percent free power plus one percent earmarked for the Local Area Development Fund, alongside Rs 599.88 crore in budgetary support for enabling infrastructure, Rs 750 crore in central financial assistance towards the state’s equity share, and roughly 29 kilometres of new roads and bridges in Anjaw and Namsai districts, largely accessible for local use. Yet, looking beyond official projections to ecological reporting and local accounts exposes severe environmental and social costs that threaten the Lohit basin. An investigative report first published on Mongabay on 19 June, 2026, detailed how the proposed dam site in Hawai, located just 26.5 kilometres from the Namdapha Tiger Reserve and 11 kilometres from the Kamlang Wildlife Sanctuary, sits directly inside the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot and requires felling 33,338 trees across tropical wet and dense mixed forests. Beyond potential noise and water pollution, wildlife experts warned of serious risks to endemic and sensitive species such as the takin (for which the environmental impact assessment proposes a Rs 100 lakh conservation plan covering habitat protection, anti-poaching, monitoring, research, training, and awareness), the large Indian civet, the Assamese macaque, and the jungle cat. Most critically, the project endangers the white-bellied heron, a critically endangered bird listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act. With fewer than 60 individuals estimated globally in 2015 and only six to nine remaining in Arunachal, the species depends on clear, shallow, fast-flowing river streams to forage for fish and struggles to adapt when river habitats are altered. The urgency of protecting the Lohit’s riverine habitat was brought into sharp focus on 12 November, 2026, when the white-bellied heron research team of the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) recorded a sighting of the bird along the Lohit River, noting that fewer than 10 individuals are believed to survive in the wild in India, and that undisturbed Eastern Himalayan riverine habitats are vital to its survival.
